channel.title: Dr. Caner Özyıldırım — Scientific Articles
channel.description: Evidence-based scientific essays and clinical reviews on metabolism, obesity etiology, and nutrition.

item.title: Is Sleep Poised to Become a Dietary Risk Factor?
item.description: Nutritional science can no longer be confined to what lies on the dinner plate. Controlled metabolic trials show that sleep restriction elevates caloric intake, stimulates hedonic appetite, and causes weight loss during dieting to derive disproportionately from lean muscle rather than body fat.

item.title: Fasting While Having Insulin Resistance May Not Be Such a Good Idea
item.description: Two individuals follow the exact same intermittent fasting regimen for the same duration. One loses visceral fat and narrows their waistline; the other sees the scale drop, yet abdominal adiposity persists. Emerging evidence suggests hyperinsulinemia fundamentally shifts how the body responds to fasting.

item.title: Intermittent Fasting Isn't Working for You? Your Gut Microbiome Might Be the Reason
item.description: You adhere strictly to your fasting windows and eat mindfully, yet fail to see the promised metabolic rewards? The bottleneck may not reside in your cells, but within the microscopic ecosystem of your gut flora.

item.title: Your Diet May Be Epigenetically Programming Your Liver for Cancer Years in Advance
item.description: Years of consuming high-fat, ultra-processed diets can fundamentally alter the identity and epigenetic state of hepatocytes—long before any somatic oncogenic mutations occur. Discover how diet writes the pre-cancerous playbook.

item.title: Can Nutrients Naturally Stimulate GLP-1? The Science of Dietary Incretin Secretion
item.description: From viral 'Oat-zempic' trends to berberine supplements, social media claims nature has its own GLP-1 agonists. What does biochemistry actually say about nutrient-stimulated incretin release?

item.title: There Is a Subset of Patients Resistant to GLP-1 Therapies: Why Do Some Not Respond?
item.description: While incretin mimetics are celebrated as clinical breakthroughs, clinical trials prove that roughly 10-15% of patients experience minimal to zero weight loss. What causes GLP-1 resistance?

item.title: How Does a Blood Sugar-Raising Hormone Promote Weight Loss? The Paradox of Glucagon
item.description: In classical textbooks, glucagon was labeled the 'evil' counterpart to insulin that raises blood glucose. Why is the newest generation of obesity medications deliberately incorporating glucagon agonism?

item.title: The GLP-1 Exit Strategy: What Actually Happens When You Discontinue Incretin Therapy?
item.description: What happens when patients reach their target weight and discontinue incretin therapy? Exploring the biological weight regain recoil and building a clinically viable de-escalation protocol.

item.title: The Muscle Mass Panic with GLP-1: Are We Losing Muscle or Shrinking Overall Body Mass?
item.description: Alarmist headlines claim GLP-1 medications melt away skeletal muscle. What does DEXA body composition data actually show? Distinguishing between the 'Quarter Rule' and pathological sarcopenia.

item.title: GLP-1 Agonists: Is Weight Loss the Same as Truly Treating the Disease of Obesity?
item.description: Do incretin medications actually cure obesity or merely induce substantial mass reduction? Deconstructing the five foundational pillars of modern obesity medicine.

item.title: Feeling Full on GLP-1 Doesn't Change the Fact That Your Cells Might Be Starving
item.description: When incretin medications completely turn off hunger, patients often celebrate surviving on a coffee and a single cracker. But cellular starvation and micronutrient collapse are a silent clinical hazard.
